title: Finite locally free degree survives flat first-order deformation
statement: Let $S_0\hookrightarrow S'$ be a first-order thickening of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Let $q':V'\to S'$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism], and put $q_0:V_0=S_0\times_{S'}V'\to S_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every integer $d\geq0$, if $q_0$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free], then $q'$ is finite locally free of degree $d$. No finite-presentation, quasi-compactness, Noetherian hypothesis, or finiteness assumption on the square-zero ideal is imposed in advance.

source.place: Tag 06AG (lemma-deform-property), part item-finite-locally-free (23), with Y prime = S prime and Y = S; fixed degree follows from the identical residue-field fibres.

proof.text: By [def-pc-finite-locally-free], $q_0$ is finite and locally of finite presentation. The first-order hypothesis means $\mathcal I^2=0$, hence is a finite-order thickening with $n=1$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-finite-cartesian] to $S_0\subset S'$ and $V_0=S_0\times_{S'}V'$: it gives that $q'$ is finite. Its flatness is already a hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, Ad (23), using Ad (22); Tag 09ZW, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian (8)

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U'=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](1), $U_0=S_0\times_{S'}U'$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, with $I$ the defining ideal; $I^2=0$ by [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Put $W'=V'\times_{S'}U'$. Its map to $U'$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Its reduction is $W_0=V_0\times_{S_0}U_0$: indeed a map to either iterated fibre product consists of maps to $V'$, $S_0$ and $U'$ with the same image in $S'$, so the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives mutually inverse maps. The map $W_0\to U_0$ is locally of finite presentation: every affine open of $W_0$, viewed as an open of $V_0$, lies over the affine open $U_0$ of $S_0$, so [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] for $q_0$ supplies its finite presentation over $A/I$, and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] applies. Now [lem-sfb-flat-deformation-lfp] with $Y=W'$, base ring $A$ and exponent $N=2$ shows that $W'\to U'$ is locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, general remark (I) and Ad (13), applied on affine opens of the base

proof.text: Every $v'\in V'$ maps into an affine open $U'$ of $S'$. The local finite presentation from step 2 supplies affine neighbourhoods of $v'$ and $q'(v')$ with a finitely presented coordinate-ring map. These are also open neighbourhoods in $V'$ and $S'$, so [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] proves that $q'$ is locally of finite presentation. Step 1 and the assumed flatness now give all three conditions defining finite locally free in [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, Ad (23); Tag 02KB, morphisms-lemma-finite-flat, using the project definition of finite locally free

proof.text: It remains to check degree. Given $s'\in S'$, the homeomorphism in [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] gives its unique preimage $s_0\in S_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso], the induced map $\kappa(s')\to\kappa(s_0)$ is an isomorphism. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $V_0\times_{S_0}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_0)$ with $V'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_0)$: maps to either side are precisely compatible maps to $V'$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_0)$. Using the residue-field isomorphism, this is the fibre of $q'$ at $s'$. These isomorphisms respect the structure maps to the residue-field spectra, hence identify their global-section algebras over the identified fields. A vector-space basis transfers along these inverse isomorphisms, so their dimensions agree. The fibre of $q_0$ has dimension $d$ by hypothesis and [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Therefore every fibre of $q'$ has dimension $d$, proving the asserted degree. This also covers $d=0$; if $S'$ is empty the fibre condition is vacuous.
